guide.title: User Guide
guide.subtitle: Translate Google Slides, Docs, Sheets and Forms into another language — the layout stays, and your original is never changed.
guide.start.lead: Takes about a minute. A free Gemini key needs no credit card and gives natural, high-quality translations.
guide.start.s1.p: Open a Google Slides, Docs, Sheets or Forms file, then click the Workspace Translator Pro icon in the Chrome toolbar. Don't see it? Click the puzzle-piece icon and pin it.
guide.start.s2.h: Get an API key — Gemini recommended
guide.start.s2.p: We recommend Gemini: it's free to use — a free tier with no credit card. The first time, {quickSetup} opens in the panel. Click {openStudio}, sign in with your Google account, click “Create API key” and copy the key.
guide.start.s3.p: Paste the key into the box. It is checked and saved automatically; when the green confirmation appears, click {start}.
guide.start.free: Don't want a key? Choose {useFree} at the bottom of {quickSetup}. It works without a key, but the quality is lower and translation preferences don't apply.
guide.start.auth.p: On your first translation Google asks for permission to use Drive, Slides, Docs, Sheets and Forms. The extension needs it to make a copy of your file and write the translation into that copy. If Google shows a warning that it hasn't verified the app, click “Advanced” and continue to Workspace Translator Pro.
guide.tr.lead: Everything happens in the side panel next to your open file.
guide.tr.s2: Optional — need several languages? Open {multi} and tap the languages you want. One copy is made per language.
guide.tr.s3: Optional, Slides only — {slides}: enter slide numbers such as 3-10, 12. Leave it empty to translate every slide.
guide.tr.s4: Optional, Sheets only — {sheet}: tick it to translate only the sheet tab you are looking at.
guide.tr.s5: Optional — {fileTerms}: words that need special handling in this file only (see Translation preferences).
guide.tr.s6: Click {translate}. The progress bar shows the current batch and the time left.
guide.tr.bg: You can close the side panel while it works — a notification tells you when it's done. Don't close the file's browser tab: that cancels the job. Click {stop} to cancel yourself; the unfinished copy is then deleted.
guide.tr.done: When it's finished, the {done} card shows how many text segments were translated and how long it took, with a link to every copy. The translated copy also opens automatically — turn this off in Settings → {after}.
guide.tr.where: Where is the copy? In the same Drive folder as the original, named “[Translated - language] original name”. Every copy is also listed under {history} (clock icon at the top).
guide.tr.fit: Longer text: with {fit} switched on (default), slide fonts shrink a little where the translation no longer fits, and spreadsheet columns get wider (up to a limit) or wrap the text.
guide.pr.lead: Open Settings (gear icon) → {section}. These apply to the AI engines only. Click {save} when you're done — a note reminds you if you forget.
guide.pr.tone: {tone} — {toneKeep} keeps the tone of your original. Or choose formal, neutral or casual.
guide.pr.names: {names} — for people's names, company/brand/product names and place names, choose {mTranslate}, {mKeep} or {mAnnotate}. The small example under each option shows the result. You don't have to list any names: the AI recognises them. Default: people and brands keep the original, places are translated.
guide.pr.terms: {terms} — for individual words that must always be handled the same way. Type the word as it appears in the file, then choose {termTranslate} plus the translation, or {termKeep}. The capitalisation used in your file is preserved.
guide.pr.custom: {custom} — up to 500 characters, in any language, e.g. “The readers are Japanese clients; keep sentences short.” Instructions can't change the output format; if one breaks it, it is skipped and the result card tells you.
guide.pr.preview: {preview} sums up every active rule in plain language, so you can check before translating.
guide.en.lead: Choose the engine in Settings → {engine}. After entering a key, click {test}. Translation starts only when the status shows {active}.
guide.en.gemini.p: Free to use: a free tier with no credit card. Keys start with “AIza…” or “AQ.…”. Default model: gemini-3.1-flash-lite.
guide.en.custom.p: Any OpenAI-compatible service, such as a company gateway or a model running on your own computer. Enter its address under {customUrl}; Chrome asks once for permission to reach it when you click {test}.
guide.en.free.p: No key needed. Lower quality, and translation preferences don't apply.
guide.en.model: Model names change over time. If you see “model not found”, open the provider's model list and enter a current name under {model}.
guide.en.privacy: Your API key is stored only in this browser and is sent only to the provider you chose.
guide.la.targets: You can translate into these languages:
guide.la.ui: The extension itself can be shown in the same 10 languages: Settings → {uiLang}.
guide.la.files.p: Google Slides, Docs, Sheets and Forms. Microsoft Office files (.pptx, .docx, .xlsx and the older .ppt, .doc, .xls) work too when opened from Google Drive — the translated copy is saved as a Google file.
guide.la.kept.p: Numbers, dates, web and e-mail addresses, codes and placeholders, plus formatting, images, tables and layout.
guide.faq.lead: When something goes wrong, the side panel explains what happened and what to do. The most common cases:
guide.faq.quota.a: Free Gemini keys have per-minute and daily limits. Wait a moment and try again, or switch engine in Settings.
guide.faq.model.a: The model was retired or mistyped. Enter a current model name in Settings, then click {test}.
guide.faq.copy.q: “Google Drive would not let you copy this file”
guide.faq.copy.a: You can only view or comment on the file, or the owner disabled copying. Ask for edit access, or use File → Make a copy and translate your copy.
guide.faq.signin.a: Click {translate} again and finish the Google sign-in window.
guide.faq.sheet.q: “Couldn't find the sheet tab you're on”
guide.faq.sheet.a: Untick {sheet} to translate the whole file, or reload the spreadsheet and try again.
guide.faq.word.q: A word was translated the wrong way
guide.faq.word.a: Add it under {terms} in Settings (all files) or in {fileTerms} on the main screen (this file only).
guide.faq.privacy.a: Only the text is sent, to the engine you chose, to be translated. Your files stay in your Google Drive, and the original is never modified.
guide.cl.lead: Version history of Workspace Translator Pro.
guide.cl.160.1: Quick setup: get a free Gemini key in about a minute, checked and saved automatically.
guide.cl.160.2: Translation preferences: tone, how to handle names (translate / keep / both), specific terms per file or for all files, and custom instructions.
guide.cl.160.3: Translate into several languages at once; translate only some slides or only the current sheet tab.
guide.cl.160.4: Progress with time remaining, a result card with links, and a notification — the side panel can be closed while it works.
guide.cl.160.5: Longer translations fit better: slide fonts shrink slightly and spreadsheet columns widen or wrap.
guide.cl.160.6: Copies are named after the real file name, also for Office files; the current sheet tab is found in .xlsx files.
guide.cl.160.7: Clearer error messages, unsaved-changes reminder in Settings, and many layout fixes in all 10 languages.
guide.cl.150.1: More reliable: long jobs keep running when the side panel is closed and resume after a browser restart; an expired Google sign-in is renewed automatically.
guide.cl.150.2: Safer: the extension no longer asks for access to all websites — a custom engine's address is approved only when you add it.
guide.cl.141.1: Supports Google AI Studio's new Gemini keys that start with “AQ.”.
guide.cl.140.1: The interface is available in 10 languages.
guide.cl.140.2: More natural translations, and automatic retries when Google services have a temporary problem.
guide.cl.130.1: Spreadsheet links and text formatting are kept; images in Forms are copied correctly.
guide.shot.caption: Example screen · the highlighted part is where to click
guide.start.s2.alt: Prefer OpenAI or Claude? Create a key on their site, then in Settings → {engine} choose the engine, paste the key and click {test}.
done.unusedTerms: terms not found in this file: {list} (check the spelling)

guide.cl.170.1: Slides: words in a different colour or style inside a sentence now move with their translation instead of being left behind on top of it.
guide.cl.170.2: Long translations shrink a little more to fit their boxes, and a new optional setting keeps translations concise. The result card reminds you to take a quick look.
done.untranslated: {n} text segments could not be translated and were left as is — try again or another model
prefs.concise.label: Keep translations concise so they fit the layout
prefs.concise.hint: Concise uses shorter wording; nothing is left out. Keep the default for contracts.
prefs.preview.concise: Translations are kept concise, close to the original length.
done.fitCheck: Font size reduced in {n} text boxes so longer translations fit. Some text may still run past its box — a quick look through the file is worth it
guide.pr.concise: Translation length — “Original” (default) or “Concise, fits layout”. Concise picks shorter wording so text fits slides more easily; nothing is left out, but phrasing becomes more compact. This is the default for all files; when translating Slides you can change it for that presentation alone on the main screen. Keep the default for contracts and other word-for-word text.
scope.concise.hint: This presentation only. Shorter wording; nothing is left out.
prefs.length.label: Translation length
guide.cl.170.3: Sheets: dropdown choices are translated together with the cells, so translated values are no longer marked invalid.
guide.cl.170.4: More dependable: an unusual AI reply no longer stops the whole job, the log shows what happened, the guide stays open while translating, and the interface and target language follow your browser's language (Traditional or Simplified Chinese by region).
prefs.group.style.desc: How the translation sounds and how long it is.
prefs.names.title: Names
prefs.names.desc: The AI recognises names by itself — just choose how each kind is handled.
prefs.terms.desc: Words that must always be handled your way. For one file only, use “Terms for this file” on the main screen.
prefs.terms.empty: No terms yet. Once added, every translation handles them your way.
prefs.custom.desc: Anything else you'd like the AI to know, in your own words.
prefs.docTerms.empty: No terms for this file yet.
guide.cl.171.1: Language names now appear in your interface language, with the native name beside them (e.g. “Japanese (日本語)”), so every language is easy to find.
settings.notifyDone: Notify me when a translation is ready
settings.notifyDone.hint: Chrome asks once for permission. Handy when the side panel is closed.
guide.cl.171.2: Completion notifications are now optional: turn them on in Settings → After Translation. Updates no longer ask for new permissions.
guide.cl.172.1: Faster translation: several parts of a file are now translated at the same time, while still staying within your AI provider's per-minute limit.
guide.cl.172.2: More reliable when many files are translated into many languages at once: saved translations and history no longer run out of space.
error.busy: {engine} is overloaded right now (a temporary problem on their side, not your quota). Parts already translated are saved — try again in a few minutes and only the rest will be translated.
guide.faq.busy.a: The AI provider's servers are busy. This is temporary and doesn't use up your quota. Parts already translated are saved, so trying again in a few minutes only translates the rest. If it keeps happening, switch to another model in Settings.
